title: The Last Inheritance
premise: Noor Zhou, cathedral archivist and unlicensed solver of the city's overlooked deaths, is hired by a nervous stranger who insists a murder is being planned — and pays handsomely to prove it hasn't happened yet. The trail leads to a thirty-year-old inheritance dispute buried beneath the cathedral's locked crypt, where three old alibis were woven together like a shroud. As Noor closes in, they realize the client is not preventing a murder but laundering one, and that their own quiet investigations made them the perfect scapegoat. In the crypt's cold dark, Noor must choose between exposing the whole rotten inheritance — destroying the innocent along with the guilty — or letting justice stay buried, and they find a third way that costs them the anonymity they built their life on.
about_author: Gideon Joubert is the pen name of a former court records clerk who spent eleven years reading the paperwork of unsolved deaths. He writes mysteries about people the system files away and forgets, and he still keeps his own locked drawer.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the cathedral archives, Noor catalogs the three deaths they quietly solved, establishing their methods and their rule: never be seen. Emotional beat: the comfort of invisible competence, shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: A Client Before the Fact
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A pale stranger named Voss arrives, pays triple in advance, and asks Noor to prove that a murder will not happen — to a man named Aldous Rehn. Noor accepts against instinct. Beat: unease dressed as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Dead Yet
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor surveils Rehn, a frail philanthropist, and finds his life suspiciously well-protected — as if someone wants him alive. Beat: the first inversion; protection reads like a cage.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Dust
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, with a brief archive flashback. Old parish records reveal a 1994 inheritance: four heirs, one drowned, one disowned. The crypt was sealed the week the will was read. Beat: the past pressing upward.

chapters.title: What the Police Called Weather
chapters.summary: Detective Ilse Brandt's POV. Brandt, who half-suspects an archivist solved her old cold cases, reopens the drowned heir's file and finds Noor's fingerprints in the margins. Beat: hunter noticing hunter.

chapters.title: The Second Heir's Alibi
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor interviews Marit Rehn, who offers an alibi so detailed it feels rehearsed — because it is; she's told it for thirty years. Beat: pity curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Voss, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor tails Voss and watches him burn papers in a public incinerator. One scrap survives: a page of the 1994 will. Beat: the client becomes a suspect.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Using archive keys, Noor enters the sealed crypt and finds the drowned heir's coffin empty, its nameplate scratched off. Beat: dread — the death they're investigating happened here.

chapters.title: Brandt Comes to the Archive
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Brandt confronts Noor with circumstantial threads, offering a bargain: help me, or become my suspect. Noor deflects. Beat: two solitary minds circling, neither trusting the other.

chapters.title: The Third Heir Speaks
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A dying heir, Tomas, confesses fragments: the will was forged, the drowned heir was alive in the crypt that night. Beat: revelation that reframes everything — the murder may be thirty years old.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven Like a Shroud
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor maps the four alibis and finds they corroborate each other in an impossible chain — each heir vouching for the next. Someone designed it. Beat: awe at the cruelty of the construction.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Marit's POV. Marit recalls the night of 1994: her brother's death staged, her silence purchased with her inheritance, her life since a slow payment. Beat: guilt as a lifelong tax.

chapters.title: A Murder Not Yet Committed
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor realizes Voss's request was a trap: proving no murder is coming would seal the official record that Rehn dies naturally — covering the old crime's loose end. Rehn is the last witness. Beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: The Empty Coffin Explained
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Records and Tomas's fragments align: the drowned heir survived, was hidden, and lived — perhaps still lives — under another name. Beat: hope, immediately shadowed by who benefits from his silence.

chapters.title: Brandt's Cold File Burns
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Someone leaks Noor's unofficial investigations to Brandt's superiors; Brandt is ordered to arrest the archivist for obstruction. Beat: betrayal — the system weaponized by the guilty.

chapters.title: Running Out of Time
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, hunted. Noor goes dark in the city they've always watched invisibly, piecing together Voss's identity: he is the drowned heir's son, paid by the heirs to end his father's testimony. Beat: paranoia sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Man in the Pew
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor finds the drowned heir — ancient, hidden for decades in the cathedral's care by a now-dead priest who kept the secret. He wants, finally, to be seen. Beat: grief and release.

chapters.title: The Confession in the Crypt
chapters.summary: Alternating Noor/Brandt POV. Noor lures Voss and Marit to the crypt with proof; Brandt, disobeying orders, follows. The heirs' chain of alibis collapses aloud. Beat: the trap inverting; truth as a weapon finally unsheathed.

chapters.title: What Voss Was Paid To Do
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Voss confesses he was hired to ensure his father's death would be ruled natural — the 'murder to prevent' was the paperwork. He breaks; Marit does not. Beat: the banality of bought silence.

chapters.title: The Third Way
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor refuses both choices — full exposure that ruins innocents, or burial that frees the guilty — and gives Brandt the forged will plus the living witness, letting the law do what Noor cannot. Beat: costly trust.

chapters.title: Arrests and Aftermath
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. The heirs are charged; Voss turns state's evidence; the old man's identity becomes headline news, ending his hidden life with dignity. Noor, exposed, is quietly cleared but no longer invisible. Beat: justice arriving, imperfect and public.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the reopened crypt, now a memorial, Noor begins a new ledger — no longer anonymous, no longer alone, with Brandt leaving a card on the archive desk. Beat: quiet resolve; the price of survival paid in visibility, and worth it.
